01-distributed-design: Two software engineers, a woman and a man in their early thirties in modern work-casual clothes, stand at the glass wall of a bright modern office overlooking a clean, sunlit parcel sorting hall; he points down at plain brown cardboard parcels passing a scanner arch on a conveyor while she holds an open laptop turned toward him and the camera, showing a softly blurred diagram of coloured boxes and arrows.
02-aspire: A software engineer in her early thirties at a bright corner desk by a window leans back with a relieved smile as the large plain white monitor in front of her, with no logo on it and angled so its screen faces the camera, shows a grid of softly blurred tiles that have all turned green, one hand still resting on the keyboard; through the window beside her, plain white delivery vans stand side-on in a sunlit depot yard, far away and softly out of focus, with no badge, emblem or number plate on them.
03-hosting: In the bright software team room of a last-mile parcel delivery company, a software engineer in her early thirties at a white standing desk presses the key that starts a cloud deployment on her plain laptop with no logo on its lid, its screen showing a softly blurred progress bar beginning to fill, while a male colleague in his late twenties beside her, coffee cup in hand, watches the screen, both smiling; on a light-oak shelf behind them stand a few plain brown parcel cartons.
04-service-bus: At a light-oak high table by a tall window in the bright software team room of a last-mile parcel delivery company, a software engineer in her early thirties holds up her phone with its screen facing the viewer, showing a softly blurred delivery progress view of three mint dots in a vertical line joined by a thin line, the third dot just lighting up, while a male colleague in his late twenties beside her rests one hand on a plain brown parcel carton on the table and smiles at the phone.
05-event-grid-hubs: A software engineer in her early thirties photographs a plain brown cardboard parcel on a light-oak desk with a plain white phone with no logo on it, while a colleague in his late twenties leans in beside her to the open laptop next to the parcel, turned so its screen faces the camera, where one new mint-green row has just appeared at the top of a softly blurred list with no letters, words or numbers anywhere; both smile, in a bright daylight office.
06-event-sourcing-cqrs: Two software engineers, a woman and a man in their early thirties in modern work-casual clothes, stand at a tall glass wall in a bright logistics software office: she presses one more orange sticky note onto the end of a long horizontal row of orange sticky notes joined by short hand-drawn arrows, the row running in from the edge of the glass and ending at her hand in the middle, while he stands close beside her holding an open laptop with its screen towards the camera and smiles. The notes are plain orange squares with no letters, words or numbers anywhere.
07-dapr: A software engineer in her early thirties in modern work-casual clothes sits in the open side door of a plain white delivery van with no lettering or logo on it, parked in a bright, modern parcel depot, a laptop with a plain lid on her knees showing a softly blurred panel of small squares, most filled mint green and one still empty, while a male colleague in his early thirties standing beside the van slides one plain brown cardboard parcel onto the shelf inside and glances at her screen, both smiling.
08-durable-execution: Two software engineers, a woman and a man in their early thirties in modern work-casual clothes, sit side by side on a light sofa in the bright office lounge of a modern parcel delivery company, leaning forward over a large sheet of white paper on the low light-oak table in front of them: she draws a curved arrow that runs back beneath a row of hand-drawn boxes joined by forward arrows and looks up at him with a smile, while he holds a coffee cup and nods; a plain brown cardboard parcel sits beside the sheet, and the sketch shows only boxes and arrows, with no letters, words or numbers anywhere.
09-ai-agents: At a white standing desk in the bright engineering room of a last-mile parcel delivery company, an Azure developer in her early thirties approves a parcel reroute with one key press on her laptop while a software architect of about thirty-five beside her watches a large plain white monitor with no logo on it, where a soft blurred map shows one van route redrawn as a mint line, with no letters, words or numbers anywhere on the screen.
